floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 11->5 with clean pure-C levers (kind-split + branch-flip); residual 5 all traces to GCC 2.7.2 CSE merging the +0x270 dual-typed read to one load (target's 2nd lhu unreachable in pure C).

frontier.hypothesis: kind-split is a sanctioned (split-init/duplicated-statement family) construct, banking floor 6 cleanly.
frontier.mechanism: Redundant-mask into a second pseudo; mirrors sibling codegen; 2026-06-15 reviewer called it dual-use with sanctioned split-init-accumulation.
frontier.next_probe: Run cheat-reviewer on the kind-split in isolation; if PASS, banked floor is 5-6 with H3.

frontier.hypothesis: A semantically-purposeful C construct keeps two HImode loads of +0x270 (union/overlapping field, or a genuine memory-invalidating op between reads).
frontier.mechanism: CSE only merges when the MEM stays available; a real intervening store or a distinct union member could keep both loads without codegen-steering.
frontier.next_probe: Inspect the entity struct layout at +0x270 for a legit dual-view field; grep other +0x270 accessors for signed+unsigned use with purpose.

frontier.hypothesis: If no natural two-load source exists, the +0x270 second-lhu gap is a reviewer-tension/ruling item (target provably contains a construct the reviewer's Test-1 rejects).
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 CSE makes the 2nd lhu unreachable from any single-purpose C; only codegen-steering reaches it, yet the shipped binary has it.
frontier.next_probe: After exhausting frontier item 2, emit ruling-request asking whether the guarded dual-typed read already in HEAD (and the target) is sanctioned for this function.
